findings.issue: The gallery tree pane renders its search box WITHOUT the Ctrl+F keyboard-hint chip, while the A05 preview's tree pane shows it at the end of the search box, and the spec names it as part of the toolbar («search input with the Ctrl+F kbd hint»). Confirmed in the running host: the toolbar markup contains no Kbd element and `.w-gallery-tree kbd` is absent. The round-1 change made ShowShortcutHint default to BindGlobalShortcut, and the gallery passes BindGlobalShortcut="false", so the only place the component is demonstrated now hides a required part of its anatomy — and it is inconsistent with the stand-alone WSearch in the same gallery (Gallery.razor line 39), which passes BindGlobalShortcut="false" and still shows the chip.
findings.fix: On the WTreeToolbar at Gallery.razor line 163 add `ShowShortcutHint="true"` beside `BindGlobalShortcut="false"`, so the gallery pane shows the same chip the A05 preview shows (this is exactly the opt-in the new nullable parameter was added for). Alternative, if a live shortcut is preferred over a demo chip: drop `BindGlobalShortcut="false"` from the WTreeToolbar so the box is really bound and the chip is honest — the other gallery search box is unbound, so nothing competes for Ctrl+F on this page.

findings.issue: The pane title is emitted as `@Title` with no bidi isolation, while every other user-visible string in the component (name, meta, state, badge) goes through Bidi.Wrap/bdi. A pane title carrying a Latin or numeric token (a unit code, a year) will reorder under the RTL paragraph direction — the failure AGREEMENT item 55 exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Render it as `<bdi class="w-tree-toolbar-text">@Bidi.Wrap(Title)</bdi>` and add `@using Wakeel.Design.Bidi` to WTreeToolbar.razor.

findings.issue: Dead caret during a search. In `Build`, `HasChildren` is taken from `sourceChildren.Count > 0`, but while a search is active the non-matching children have already been filtered out of `children`. A branch that matches on its own name therefore still renders a caret; clicking it flips aria-expanded to "true" (IsExpanded now wins in the `open` expression) while the render guard `node.Children.Count > 0` renders no group at all, so the control does nothing and the row lies to a screen reader.
findings.fix: Pass the effective child count into the node while filtering: `new Node(item, key, depth, HasSearch ? children.Count > 0 : sourceChildren.Count > 0, open, children, data)`, and keep `open` as it is.

findings.issue: `ExpandAll()` / `CollapseAll()` are `void` wrappers that discard the task (`_ = ExpandAllAsync()`), so an exception thrown inside a caller's ExpandedChanged handler is swallowed instead of reaching Blazor's error boundary — the exact defect the round-1 fix removed from SetExpanded.
findings.fix: Keep only the Async pair on the public surface (the gallery already calls ExpandAllAsync/CollapseAllAsync); if the sync wrappers must stay for existing call sites, have them `_ = InvokeAsync(ExpandAllAsync)` so the dispatcher surfaces the failure rather than dropping it.

findings.issue: Preview deviation carried over from round 1: A05 prints the move hint line («اسحب الوحدة داخل الشجرة…») inside the tree pane, under the last row; the gallery prints its equivalent («مقبض الترتيب في نهاية كل صف…») as the section sub-title above the pane. Visible as a missing in-pane footer line when the two are laid side by side.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is for the gallery (WSectionHeader is the gallery's own framing convention and the A05 screen itself will place the hint inside its pane). If exactness is wanted, move the text into the WTreeToolbar's ChildContent slot rendered after the tree, or add an optional FooterHint parameter to the toolbar.

missing_spec_items: The toolbar's «search input with the Ctrl+F kbd hint» is implemented in WTreeToolbar/WSearch but is not visible anywhere the component is demonstrated: the gallery section suppresses the hint chip (see finding 1). Every other spec item — API surface, row anatomy, states, search, ARIA, keyboard, indentation via one custom property, toolbar, four-level gallery sample in light and dark, and the bUnit list — is implemented.
